pr.title: Async drop poll shim for error dropee generates noop body
pr.description:
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/140930.

<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
<!--
    https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/126482

    r? oli-obk
-->
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

When dropee type for async drop poll shim is `ty::Error(_)`, the generated poll function will be noop body. To avoid ICE in `elaborate_drop`.
pr.author: azhogin

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: When dropee type for async drop poll shim is `ty::Error(_)`, the generated poll function will be noop body. To avoid ICE in `elaborate_drop`.

The supplied PR explicitly relates this guard to `elaborate_drop`, and inspection confirms that drop elaboration is the core of the registered `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass. The shim change prevents error dropee types from entering that shared logic.

processing.reason: The historical change is an error-recovery guard in `build_async_drop_shim`: the fixed code returns a noop shim body when `drop_ty.references_error()`, while the pre-fix path lets a `ty::Error` dropee fall through into normal async-drop shim/drop elaboration. The regression test is a compile-fail/ICE test (`open-drop-error2.rs`), and the observable historical difference is a compiler ICE during `ElaborateDrops`, not a defined runtime value difference. Any source-level pair that made the erroneous branch produce a different concrete return value would have to invent runtime behavior (or UB) for `ty::Error`; that is not the historical transformation and cannot have both executions pass Miri. Modern rustc also correctly rejects the reproducer with E0277 instead of ICE, as required. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with differing defined runtime values can be validated here.

analysis.originalLogic: `build_async_drop_shim` always built the async-drop shim when `needs_async_drop` was true, regardless of whether the dropee type was an error type. The original early-return guard was only `if !needs_async_drop { ... return body; }`, with the comment: "Returning noop body for types without `need async drop` (or sync Drop in case of !`need async drop` && `need drop`)".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to fall through from the `!needs_async_drop` check into normal async-drop shim construction when `drop_ty` was `ty::Error(_)`. That is, an erroneous dropee was treated as a valid async-droppable type instead of being short-circuited to a noop body. The PR fixes this by changing the guard to `if !needs_async_drop || drop_ty.references_error()`, so error types also return the noop body before drop elaboration. Do not model the fix as changing a valid shim's semantics; it is an error-recovery guard.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs using the unstable async-drop feature where an async drop shim is constructed for a dropee whose inferred type contains `ty::Error`. The regression test uses `async_drop_in_place(&raw mut e)` on `let mut e = wrong();`, where `wrong() -> impl Sized` returns `*"abc"` (type `str`), producing a `Sized` error. The shim is then built for the error type.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in async destructor ctor shim construction: when the dropee type references `ty::Error`, return the noop shim body instead of proceeding into async drop shim generation, preventing an ICE during ElaborateDrops. A UI regression test exercises an unsized `str` error type passed to `async_drop_in_place` under `-Zvalidate-mir -Zinline-mir=yes`.
analysis.trigger: Build an async-drop shim for a value whose type is an error type (for example, an unsized `str` inferred from an erroneous return) with `needs_async_drop == true`, causing the normal shim path to operate on `ty::Error` and the later drop elaboration to ICE.
preconditions: The `async_drop` feature is enabled (the test uses `#![feature(async_drop)]` and `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`).
`async_drop_in_place` is called on a value whose type is or references `ty::Error`.
The async-drop shim is constructed with `needs_async_drop` true, so the original `!needs_async_drop` guard does not return early.
Drop elaboration later processes the resulting body, where the error type must not be treated as a normal dropee.
pitfalls: `ty::Error` is a sentinel error-recovery type; it must not flow into normal drop elaboration as though it were a real dropee type.
Guarding only on `needs_async_drop` is insufficient: an erroneous dropee can still report needing async drop and reach shim construction.
The fix uses `drop_ty.references_error()` (requiring `TypeVisitableExt`) rather than checking only the outer type, so nested error types are also caught.
The expected behavior is a normal diagnostic such as E0277 (unsized `str`), not an ICE; the noop body is error recovery, not a claim that the erroneous program is valid.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI compile-fail regression test (`tests/ui/async-await/async-drop/open-drop-error2.rs`) with compile flags `-Zvalidate-mir -Zinline-mir=yes --crate-type=lib`, enable `async_drop`, and create an error-typed dropee via `fn wrong() -> impl Sized { *"abc" }`; pass it to `async_drop_in_place`, pin the future, and call `i.poll(context)`. Check that the only error is `E0277` ("the size for values of type `str` cannot be known at compilation time") and that there is no ICE. The MIR-validation and inlining flags help exercise the shim/drop-elaboration path. Also compare stderr against the checked-in `.stderr` file.
